note: Tajikistan: by the Consular Department's own country data, behind its 'Check if you need visa' page (ordinary passports): nationals of the countries listed enter without a visa, some with no limit (Belarus, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia, Ukraine and North Korea), others for 90, 30 or 14 days; those listed for it get a visa on arrival at Dushanbe airport (no length given) and the rest listed an e-Visa (up to 60 days); everyone else (Afghanistan, Myanmar, Nepal, Zambia and others) needs a visa from a mission. Read on 2026-11-03; it corrected Wikipedia's copy, read before, at many points: a 14-day exemption for China, Vietnam, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Albania, North Macedonia, Fiji and others, Ukraine and Moldova without limit, Dominica 14 days not 90, Grenada and Suriname 90 days, a visa on arrival open to about 140 nationalities (the 45 days, Morocco's 2 months and Iran's 90-day window, which the data doesn't give, were dropped), and the mission visa for those with neither an e-Visa nor a visa on arrival, which the file had taken as an e-Visa for every other passport. The Gorno-Badakhshan permit isn't modelled.
